README.md.overview: Contract for the page. Tour step 1. One site, a 30-day window, CSV or PDF after a load. Flags are not a link budget and not a navigation aid.

sections.title: What a load covers
sections.explanation: States the window: 15 days before today and today through the next 14 days. The page opens on latitude -20.04, longitude -39.52, times in America/Sao_Paulo. Nothing is fetched until Load 30 days. Missing values stay Unavailable.

sections.title: Sources and how to run
sections.explanation: Names the Open-Meteo forecast, archive, and marine hosts. Run is the local server. Deploy is static hosting. The license section closes the file.

index.html.overview: Dashboard shell. Tour step 2. The form holds the site. Export controls stay inactive until a load finishes.

sections.title: Header clock
sections.explanation: The header shows WeatherMeter, a UTC clock, and a last-fetch stamp that starts as not yet. That stamp is the visible proof a load has not happened.

sections.title: Site form
sections.explanation: The form defaults to the offshore example, latitude -20.04 and longitude -39.52, timezone America/Sao_Paulo. Find place looks up a name. South and west are negative. The map link uses the same coordinates.

sections.title: Rest of the page
sections.explanation: The remainder holds the load button, the charts, and the daily table. Those regions stay empty until the page script fills them after a successful fetch.

serve.py.overview: Static server. Tour step 2. Standard library only. It binds to loopback unless --expose is passed, and it refuses to serve .git.

sections.title: Git path block
sections.explanation: Handler extends SimpleHTTPRequestHandler. GET and HEAD that start with /.git return 404 before the parent handler runs. Query strings are stripped before that check.

sections.title: Bind policy
sections.explanation: Default bind is 127.0.0.1 and default port is 8766. A non-loopback bind without --expose is a parser error. The process serves until KeyboardInterrupt.

requirements.txt.overview: Python note. Tour step 2. There is nothing to pip install. serve.py uses the standard library. TypeScript 5.9.2 is a separate toolchain in package.json.

sections.title: No pip packages
sections.explanation: Says Python 3.9 or newer and that serve.py uses only the standard library. There are no third-party packages.

sections.title: TypeScript is separate
sections.explanation: Points at package.json for the TypeScript 5.9.2 dev dependency. That toolchain is not installed by this file.

src/window.ts.overview: Date window. Tour step 3. Builds the 30 calendar days around today in a named timezone, and labels each day past, today, or future.

sections.title: Calendar date helpers
sections.explanation: formatYmd uses Intl with the given timezone, not the host local zone. addCalendarDays shifts a YYYY-MM-DD string with UTC date math so a DST change cannot skip a day.

sections.title: The thirty days
sections.explanation: windowFor walks offsets from -15 through 14 inclusive, which is 30 dates. periodOf compares the date string to today.

src/openmeteo.ts.overview: Open-Meteo client. Tour step 3. Builds forecast, marine, archive, and geocode URLs, and chooses sea, land, or nearest cells.

sections.title: Hosts and field lists
sections.explanation: Four origins: forecast, marine, archive, and geocoding. The daily and hourly field lists are the columns the rest of the page expects. Changing a name here changes the aggregate keys.

sections.title: Cell and URL builders
sections.explanation: cellSelection returns sea, land, or nearest from the site class. marineCellSelection stays on sea even for an onshore site, which matches the README: swell still comes from the sea cell. The URL builders only assemble query strings.

sections.title: Fetch helpers
sections.explanation: sleep and errorText support the request path. Failures stay as errors. This file does not fill a missing series from another host.

src/aggregate.ts.overview: Joins the four series into one day table. Tour step 3. A missing archive or marine response stays missing. It is not copied from the forecast.

sections.title: Index helpers
sections.explanation: indexDaily and indexHours key rows by date. val returns null for a missing or non-finite number. hasCore checks the temperature, rain, and cloud fields the table cannot do without.

sections.title: Assemble one window
sections.explanation: assemble indexes forecast daily and hourly always. Archive and marine maps are built only when that host answered ok. Days the archive missed keep a null, and the UI later prints Unavailable.

src/satcom.ts.overview: Condition flags. Tour step 4. Rain, cloud, gusts, thunderstorm, and an offshore sea-state line. Thresholds are named constants. A null input does not trip a flag.

sections.title: Threshold constants
sections.explanation: Rain is 5 mm daily or 2 mm in an hour. Heavy rain is 10 mm in an hour. Cloud is 80 percent mean or 90 percent in a layer. Gusts are 30 kt. Swell is 2 m and wave is 2.5 m. Thunder codes are 95, 96, and 99.

sections.title: Flag rules
sections.explanation: maxOf ignores nulls. conditionFlags pushes a label only when a finite value crosses a threshold. The sea-state sentence is added only when site is offshore. An onshore site with a large swell gets no sea-state flag.

src/csv.ts.overview: CSV export of one loaded snapshot. Tour step 4. The header row is fixed. A null cell stays empty rather than becoming zero.

sections.title: Headers and cells
sections.explanation: HEADERS names every column. cell formats a number to a digit count, and dailyValues and hourlyValues walk one row into that column order.

sections.title: File body
sections.explanation: exportBasename uses latitude and longitude to four decimals. toCsv writes comment lines for the grids, then the header, then one line per row. A stale snapshot is marked in those comments.

src/app.ts.overview: Page controller. Tour step 4. Reads the form, calls the load, and writes charts and the table. It also remembers the last form in localStorage.

sections.title: Form read and save
sections.explanation: Storage keys are weathermeter:last, weathermeter:form, and weathermeter:theme. readForm parses latitude and longitude and returns an error string instead of throwing on a bad field. restoreForm accepts only the offshore and custom presets.

sections.title: Map refresh
sections.explanation: refreshMap parses the same lat and lon fields and updates the iframe and the open-in-maps link. A coordinate that fails to parse does not move the map.

sections.title: Load and render
sections.explanation: The rest of the file runs Load 30 days: it calls the Open-Meteo helpers, assembles the snapshot, then fills status, charts, and the table. Export stays off until that snapshot exists.

js/app.js.overview: Browser emit of app.ts. Tour step 5. The page loads this file, not the TypeScript. Behavior should match src/app.ts. If it does not, the emit is stale.

sections.title: Same form keys
sections.explanation: CACHE_KEY, FORM_KEY, and THEME_KEY match the TypeScript. readForm and restoreForm use the same preset check. This is the file the browser executes.

sections.title: Map and the rest
sections.explanation: refreshMap and the load handler mirror src/app.ts. Edit the TypeScript and re-emit. Do not patch this file alone or the next build will overwrite it.

js/openmeteo.js.overview: Browser emit of openmeteo.ts. Tour step 5. The four Open-Meteo origins and the URL builders are the same names as the TypeScript.

sections.title: Origins and fields
sections.explanation: Forecast, marine, archive, and geocode origins, plus cellSelection. The field arrays are what the aggregate keys against.

sections.title: URL builders
sections.explanation: forecastUrl, marineUrl, archiveUrl, and geocodeUrl build query strings. sleep and errorText support retries. This file does not invent a value when a host fails.

js/aggregate.js.overview: Browser emit of aggregate.ts. Tour step 5. assemble joins forecast, archive, and marine. A host that did not answer leaves nulls.

sections.title: Row indexes
sections.explanation: indexDaily, indexHours, and hourMap key the series. val returns null for a bad number. aside formats an archived row and prints Unavailable for a null.

sections.title: Assemble
sections.explanation: assemble is the export the page calls after the fetches. Archive and marine contribute only when their response was ok.

tests/aggregate.test.js.overview: node:test for assemble. Tour step 6. A fixed clock of 2026-09-29 builds a window, then checks past, today, archive, and marine rows.

sections.title: Fixture builders
sections.explanation: now is a fixed UTC instant. series and endpoint build the daily and hourly shapes assemble expects. baseInput fills a zero weather grid so each test overrides one host.

sections.title: Past, today, marine
sections.explanation: The first snapshot checks the past day and today. A later snapshot feeds an archive only for dates before 2026-09-29. Offshore and onshore snapshots check that marine data follows the site class.

tests/satcom.test.js.overview: node:test for the flag thresholds. Tour step 6. One helper builds a quiet offshore day. Each assertion crosses exactly one threshold.

sections.title: Quiet input
sections.explanation: input() returns a calm offshore day: no rain, low cloud, light gust, small swell. overrides replace one field per assertion.

sections.title: One threshold each
sections.explanation: Rain at 5 mm daily or 2 mm hourly flags Rain on the path. 10 mm hourly also flags Heavy rain. Cloud 80, a low layer at 90, gust 30, and code 95 each add their label. Swell of 2 m flags sea state only offshore. An onshore site with a large swell does not. An untouched input returns no flags.

package.json.overview: Manifest. Tour step 6. Version 1.0.0. build is tsc. test is tsc then node --test. The only dev dependency is TypeScript 5.9.2.

sections.title: Name and scripts
sections.explanation: Package name rhuanssauro-weathermeter, MIT, type module. test compiles first, so a type error fails the suite before node:test runs.

sections.title: TypeScript pin
sections.explanation: typescript is pinned at 5.9.2. There is no runtime dependency. The page is the emitted JavaScript plus the Python server.
